Units that could not be fitted

Source: R/failures.R
failures.Rd

Returns the failure table of a result: one row per unit (person, window, model or resample) whose estimation failed or was skipped, with the reason. Persons with too few complete training or held-out occasions, for example, receive no person-specific model and are listed here instead of being dropped silently.

Usage

failures(x, model = NULL, scope = NULL, subject = NULL, ...)

# Default S3 method
failures(x, model = NULL, scope = NULL, subject = NULL, ...)

Arguments

x

A result that records failures, such as a fit from fit_lm(), fit_glm(), fit_within_between(), fit_ml() or fit_effects(), a subgroup result from find_subgroups(), a rolling network result, or a model comparison.

model, scope, subject

Optional filters, applied when the table has the matching column.

...

Ignored.

Value

A base data.frame with one row per failed unit. For model fits the columns are scope, model, estimator, subject and message; other results keep the identifying columns of their own units and a message column. A result without failures returns a table with zero rows.

Errors

Raises an error of class idiographic_no_failure_table when x keeps no failure table.

Examples

# Aisha keeps only 8 days, too few for a person-specific model.
short <- subset(srl, name != "Aisha" | day <= 8)
fit <- fit_lm(short, y = "effort", x = "efficacy", id = "name",
              time = "day", scope = "individual")
failures(fit)
#>   scope  model estimator subject
#> 1 split .split    .split   Aisha
#>                                                        message
#> 1 Insufficient complete rows (train = 6, valid = 0, test = 2).
